disclaimer.title: Screening only — not a decision
text: This tool gives a rough 'you may qualify' estimate based on a few answers. It is NOT an application, a legal opinion, or an eligibility determination. Only the agency that runs each program can decide.
Results never mean you are not allowed to apply. Anyone can apply for any program, and we encourage you to.
Your answers stay in your browser by default. Nothing is sent to Root to Rise or stored unless you choose to share it.
We do not store health information (pregnancy, disability, Medicare, recovery status) without your explicit, separate consent.
Income limits change every year. Figures here were checked against official sources on the 'as of' dates shown.
Root to Rise / Inspiration Is Everywhere (EIN 82-5186366) is a community nonprofit, not a government agency.

federal_poverty_guidelines_2026.basis: 100% HHS poverty guideline, 48 contiguous states + DC

questions.text: Which state do you live in?
How many people live with you and share food/expenses (including you)?
questions.help: For WIC and MassHealth, a pregnant person counts the unborn baby(ies) — the screener adds this automatically if you say you're pregnant.

questions.text: About how much money does your household get each month before taxes? (jobs, Social Security, SSI/SSDI, unemployment, child support, etc.)
Is anyone in your household 60 or older, or getting disability benefits?
Is anyone in your household pregnant?
If pregnant: how many babies are expected?
Has anyone had a baby in the last 12 months (or is breastfeeding)?
Are there children under age 5 in your household?
Are there children under age 19 in your household?
Does anyone in your household already get any of these?

rules.logic: If household receives SSI, TANF/TAFDC/EAEDC -> may_qualify (categorical). Else if gross monthly income <= gross_limit_200 -> may_qualify. Else if has_elderly_or_disabled_member -> check_with_program (no gross income test; asset + net income tests apply). Else -> might_not_qualify_income.

categorical_shortcuts.note: Households where all members receive SSI or TANF-funded cash may be 'categorically eligible' (federal rule).

broad_based_categorical_eligibility.elderly_disabled_rule: No gross income test for households with a member 60+ or getting disability-based benefits; they must meet net income test (and asset test if gross > 200% FPL).

gross_limit_200.basis: 200% FPL gross monthly (MA broad-based categorical eligibility)
gross_limit_200.effective: Effective 2026-02-01 (based on 2026 HHS poverty guidelines). Also shown on DTA SNAP page.
gross_limit_200.note: MA updates this chart when new poverty guidelines publish (usually Feb). Stays valid into FFY2027 until DTA revises it.

max_benefit_1_person.note: FDPIR home-care meal deduction equals the 48-state 1-person SNAP maximum for FY2027.

fy2027_update.max_benefit_other_sizes_note: Not verified on an official page we could access on 2026-09-26 (USDA memo PDF blocked). Third-party sites report $1,023 for 4 people — do not display until verified.
fy2027_update.ma_200pct_chart_note: No new MA 200% chart announced as of 2026-09-26; the Feb 2026 chart already uses 2026 poverty guidelines.

non_financial_notes: Work rules for able-bodied adults without dependents changed under the 2025 federal law (One Big Beautiful Bill Act); FNS says it is updating guidance. Do not screen on work rules.
Some non-citizens are not eligible; SNAP is not part of the public charge test in MA (per DTA).

rules.logic: Already has Medicaid -> may_qualify (keep coverage, renew). Adults 19–64: income <= adult_133_plus5 -> may_qualify. Pregnant: household size + expected babies; income <= pregnant_200_plus5 -> may_qualify. Children under 19: income <= children_300_plus5 -> may_qualify (children may qualify even if parents don't). Disability: CommonHealth has no upper income limit -> may_qualify (premium may apply). Age 65+: income <= seniors_100_plus20 -> may_qualify (asset limits apply); else if <= msp_qi_225_plus20 -> may_qualify for Medicare Savings Program (1–2 person only). Otherwise might_not_qualify_income and point to Health Connector.
rules.income_counting_note: MassHealth uses MAGI income (roughly taxable income) and subtracts 5 percentage points of FPL. Tables below already include the 5% deduction (MLRI table built from MassHealth desk guide).

pregnant_200_plus5.note: Add the expected baby(ies) to household size.

msp_qi_225_plus20.basis: 225% FPL + $20 (Medicare Savings Program – QI; no asset test since 2024-03-01)

commonhealth_disability.note: For people with disabilities, CommonHealth has no upper income level; premium above 150% FPL.

base_fpl_chart.note: Official MassHealth 2026 income standards chart (100/133/150/190/200/.../400% FPL, without the 5% deduction).

fy2027_update.note: MassHealth updates income standards each March 1 (next: 2027-03-01). No October change.

rules.health_connector_note: Health Connector (ConnectorCare) uses 2025 FPL for 2026 coverage; enhanced premium tax credits expired 2025-12-31 (per MLRI table).

programs.name: NH Medicaid incl. Granite Advantage Health Care Program

rules.logic: Already has Medicaid -> may_qualify. Adults 19–64, not pregnant, not on Medicare: income <= granite_advantage_133 + five_pct_disregard -> may_qualify. Pregnant (size + babies) or children under 19: income <= children_pregnant_196 + five_pct -> may_qualify; children up to expanded_cm_318 -> may_qualify (Expanded Children's Medicaid). Age 65+ or disability: different (non-MAGI) rules -> check_with_program. Otherwise might_not_qualify_income and point to HealthCare.gov.

five_pct_disregard.note: 5% MAGI deduction applied when someone otherwise fails the income test (effective limit ~138% FPL).

granite_advantage_conditions: Not entitled to/enrolled in Medicare Part A or B
Not eligible for mandatory Medicaid (e.g., APTD/ANB)
rules.work_requirement_note: Federal Medicaid work/community-engagement requirements for expansion adults (2025 law) are scheduled to begin later; NH rules may change. Do not screen on work status.

fy2027_update.note: NH updates Medicaid limits with new FPG (next ~March 2027). No October change.

rules.logic: Annual gross income (monthly*12) <= smi_60_fy2027 -> may_qualify; else might_not_qualify_income. Heating season Nov 1–Apr 30; applications open Oct 1.

smi_60_fy2027.basis: 60% of estimated MA State Median Income (FY2027 = 2026–2027 heating season)
smi_60_fy2027.note: Sizes 11–17 from MASSCAP FY2027 chart; households 18+ contact EOHLC/local agency.

rules.smi_60_fy2026_note: FY2026 (2025–26 season) limits were superseded on mass.gov by FY2027; not re-verified. Season is over, so FY2027 figures are the ones to use from Oct 1 2026.

local_administrator.cape_cod: South Shore Community Action Council (SSCAC) is the HEAP administering agency for Cape Cod & the Islands — NOT Housing Assistance Corporation (HAC runs energy-efficiency/heating system programs).

programs.name: RAFT – Residential Assistance for Families in Transition (MA emergency housing costs)

rules.logic: If housing_crisis (eviction notice, Notice to Quit, behind on mortgage, utility shutoff notice, unsafe home) -> check_with_program (income must be under 50% of the town's Area Median Income, or 60% AMI if at risk of domestic violence; AMI varies by town so the screener cannot compute it). rules.income_limit_note: 50% AMI (60% AMI with DV risk); AMI varies by city/town (Barnstable County vs. other areas). Use the state's AMI lookup / eligibility checker linked on the RAFT page — not stored here to avoid stale numbers.
